decisions.decision: Phase 5 should not use rigid parser-first document modeling as the primary approach.
decisions.rationale: The user wants Kairos to exploit LLM document reading/writing flexibility rather than replacing hardcoded templates with equally rigid schemas.

decisions.decision: Phase 5 should use prompt-governed document protocols: documents are the facts, prompts are the protocol, code is a thin guardrail.
decisions.rationale: This preserves flexibility across code and non-code tasks while keeping enough structure for continuation and auditability.

decisions.decision: Phase 5 execution should proceed in order 05A -> 05B -> 05C.
decisions.rationale: Kairos must first learn stable document generation/reading/updating before it can safely absorb user requirements and then autonomously discover spawned work.

next_action: Resume with 05A Task 1: write failing tests for the prompt-governed document protocol anchors before implementing any document protocol helpers.
context_notes: Phase 4 is closed. Phase 5 planning is now complete enough to execute. The most important design correction in this session was shifting from parser-first document modeling to an LLM-first document protocol: Kairos should generate, read, and update normalized work docs through prompts, with code only providing directory boundaries, audit, and thin safety checks. Do not jump directly to requirement execution; start with 05A document protocol primitives and tests. Avoid staging private_key.yaml.
